title: Connection Shepherd and Session Quarantine play to contain 5xx/timeouts during customer escalations
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: During the recent customer escalation we observed correlated 5xx waves and long-tail timeouts caused by a combination of connection stacking, aggressive client retries, and synchronous KV cache compaction. This ticket implements a short-term, low-risk mitigation (Connection Shepherd + Session Quarantine) and the rollout/runbook to stop amplification while we deliver longer-term fixes.
acceptance_criteria: Connection Shepherd pilot running in front of edge-proxy in canary region and correctly tracking per-session state
Per-session retry quota enforced: clients that exceed X rapid retries receive 429/503 fallback instead of being forwarded to runtime
Session Quarantine causes affected tenant requests to be routed to fast-degrade model variant or cached prefix path without causing cross-tenant impact
End-to-end dashboards show reduced request fanout and a 60-80% drop in tenant-concurrent-inflight spikes for canary tenants
Kill-switch and emergency rollback implemented with <= 2 minute effect time and clear runbook steps
updates: 2026-03-11: Incident triage. Root-cause hypothesis: connection stacking + retry amplification + KV cache compaction. Logged as high priority and assigned to oncall engineering lead (Carlos Rivera).

2026-03-12: Design review with SRE and Runtime teams. Agreed on a small new component (Connection Shepherd) to live in the edge layer to track session token, socket lifetime and retry counts. Decided to call the per-session isolation mechanism 'quarantine' to avoid confusion with tenant quarantine used elsewhere.

2026-03-13: Prototype implemented: edge sidecar exposes per-session counter keyed by request-id header; adds short-lived admission decisions. Integration tests added for rapid retry patterns. Initial canary scheduled for region us-west-2 with 5 test tenants.

2026-03-14: Canary rollout started for 5 tenants. Early telemetry shows reduced backend fanout by ~52% for those tenants. Noted a race where streaming keepalive probes were counted as retries; updated filter to ignore keepalive heartbeats.
Action items: finalize safe default retry quota, add replay-safe idempotency token check, and script the rollback (remove sidecar routing) for emergency disable.
postmortem_actions: Schedule work to refactor KV compaction triggers so full compactions are serialized and do not coincide with spike windows
Add server-side idempotency guidance and SDK improvements to back off jitter for streaming calls
Expand session quarantine to support prioritized fastpath for paid customers (policy work)
Add automated runbook play to toggle Connection Shepherd per-region via feature flag
notes: Design decisions: 1) Keep Connection Shepherd out of the hot request path by performing a cheap admission check in the edge; 2) Use token fingerprinting to avoid client-side nonce collisions; 3) Map streaming heartbeats to 'non-counted' events to prevent false positives. Operationally we prefer a per-session quota (e.g., 6 rapid retries within 30s) versus per-tenant immediate throttle to preserve good clients during noisy neighbors.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: deploy sidecar in canary region to 5 tenants (3/14). Monitor for 48h. Phase 2: expand to 20 tenants and enable fast-degrade routing for quarantined sessions. Phase 3: global rollout with staged ramp and automated rollback window. Emergency rollback: disable sidecar routing via feature flag and flush session-state.
